transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess I'm just having some trouble lately. It's... my face. 

The left side of it just looks off to me. Like my nose and my jaw are crooked. I see it every time I look at my ID photos, or... if I have to have my camera on for online classes. Other people say they don't see it, but... I don't know. When I'm in the CNC lab, I just feel like everyone is noticing it. Like they see my face being messed up before they even look at my work. 

So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Do you think your face is actually crooked, or is it just that you feel like it looks that way to others?
Um... I think it actually is. I mean, I can see it. So... yeah. It's not just a feeling. I think it's really crooked.
Does your face always look crooked to you, or are there times when it looks normal?
Um... it always looks like that. I mean, maybe sometimes it's worse than others, but... it's never normal. It's always there.
Do you think people are judging you because of how your face looks?
I mean... yeah, probably. I don't know for sure, but... it's hard not to think that. They probably are.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time thinking about your face or trying to fix how it looks?

Yeah... I guess so. Um... especially before I leave for school. I just... get stuck checking it. Like in the bathroom mirror, or... on my phone camera. I try to fix my hair or keep changing shirts to try and hide the angle. I don't know. Sometimes I ask my mom if it looks weird. 

It just... takes a while. Sometimes I do it for so long that I end up missing my lab... or I just show up and I'm too wiped out to even focus.
Has there ever been a time when you didn't think your face was crooked?

Um... no, not really. It's been a while. I mean, that's kind of why I'm here. I just... I can't stop thinking about it. Every time I see my ID photo, or when I have to turn my camera on for online classes... the left side just looks wrong. Like my nose and jaw are completely crooked. 

People tell me they don't see it, but... I don't believe them. Even when I'm in the CNC lab, I just feel like everyone is staring at my face instead of looking at my work. So... no, it's always there.
Does your concern about your face looking crooked ever change depending on how you're feeling or what's going on around you?
Um... I don't think so. I haven't really noticed it changing. It's just... pretty much always the same, I guess.
Is it just your face that you're concerned about, or are there other parts of your body that you worry about as well?
Um... no. Just my face. That's... that's the only thing.
Do you think it's possible that your face might not be as crooked as you think it is?
Um... no. I mean... I look in the mirror and I see it. It's... it's just there. I don't really see how it could be any different than what I'm seeing.
Has your concern about your face affected your relationships with friends or family?

Um... yeah, I guess. I mean, I don't really see my friends much anymore. I stopped playing soccer... and I used to volunteer, but I just... I don't want to be around people. I don't want them looking at me. And, um... it's messing up my school stuff, too. I've missed some of my CNC labs... and my shop shifts. I just couldn't leave the house. My mentor said my work placement might get pulled if I keep it up. So... yeah. It affects things.
Do you think it's possible that someone else, like a doctor or a plastic surgeon, might look at your face and not see the crookedness you see?
Um... I don't know. I mean, I guess they might not care as much, but... they'd still see it. It's pretty obvious.
Do you think there's any possibility that your face is actually normal and you're just perceiving it as crooked?
Um... no. I don't think so. I mean... I'm not making it up. I know what I see.
Do you think you would believe someone if they showed you a picture of yourself where your face looked normal?
I mean... I don't know. If the picture looked normal, I'd probably just think it was... the lighting or the angle or something. Because... it's not normal in real life.
Do you think your face would still look crooked to you even if multiple doctors told you that there's nothing wrong with it?
Um... yeah. Probably. I mean... they can say whatever they want, but... it doesn't change what's actually there. I'd still see it.
Was there something that happened that made you first notice your face looked crooked to you?
Um... no. Not really. I just... I don't know, I just started noticing it one day. There wasn't like... an event or anything. It's just always been like this, I guess.
Was your concern about your face being crooked triggered by something specific that happened to you?
I mean... like I just said, no. Nothing happened. There wasn't any kind of trigger or anything.
Do you think you would still worry about your face if you were alone all the time and never saw yourself in mirrors or photos?
I don't know. I guess... maybe? I mean, I'd still know it's there. Even if I couldn't see it, I'd know.
Do you think your face could ever look normal to you, even if you made some changes to how you take care of it or present yourself?
I don't think so. I mean... no matter what I do, it's still my face. Changing my hair or... or whatever isn't going to fix the actual problem. It's just... broken.
Is there a particular social situation where you feel more self-conscious about your face?

I mean... I guess it's worse when I'm at work. In the CNC lab. I just... I feel like everyone there is looking at it. Like they notice my crooked jaw and my nose before they even look at the parts I'm programming. And... online classes are bad too. The camera... it just makes the left side of my face look so off. Like in my ID photo. People say they don't see it, but... I know they do.
